reason: A fix to Metaform's link code landed at 18:32 local, but mcp serve and dispatch runners started before it kept the old moving-link code. The old code made `code` reappear on the map at 22:41Z. The class is any long-running process checked after a code change, and no existing skill says to compare process start times with file times.

The episode showed a stale MCP server silently running pre-fix link logic and moving a ref; the agent then switched to the CLI because it ran current code. The skill covered checks but not writes made through a stale server.

On 2026-10-15 an agent's dispatch_link through a pre-fix MCP server re-created a base element `code` and moved a ref; other agents' stale servers were the same cause. The episode showed each agent's server staying stale until its session restarts, and a leftover empty element the base would not remove. The existing skill covers the stale-write case but not the per-agent scope or the leftover element.

Rich reported a removed element ("Guy s code is back why"). The agent traced stores, a fresh process and the page for many turns before asking where he saw it. Its own earlier finding was that a process started before the fix still ran the old link code and was the likely writer. The skill should say to identify the writer from the ops log first, and to check the surface the person names before more tracing.

A removed 'code' element kept coming back. The agent found a stale pre-fix MCP server re-creating it, and also found live work and work_links rows still naming the removed id. The skill covers writer-tracing but not checking dangling records after a removal.
